Review response management

Review responses that win over the next customer

Replies to your reviews, good and bad, that show future customers how you handle people, for businesses in Denton and DFW.

What this is

The audience for a review reply is not the reviewer. It is the next person reading, deciding whether to call you.

That reframe changes everything about how replies get written, and it is the whole service in one sentence.

What you get

What responding covers

  • 01

    Every review answered

    Including the short positive ones. A profile where only the complaints have replies looks defensive; one where everything gets a reply looks like a business that is paying attention.

  • 02

    Replies that are not identical

    Fifteen reviews all answered with "Thanks for your feedback!" is worse than not replying. It reads as automated because it is.

  • 03

    Negative reviews handled properly

    Acknowledge, take it offline, stay calm. Never argue, never blame the customer, and never reveal details about their job in a public reply.

  • 04

    A view on the unfair ones

    Reviews from people who were never customers, or which breach Google's policies, can be reported. Success is far from guaranteed, and the reply matters more than the appeal.

  • 05

    Timely responses

    Days rather than months. A reply arriving a year later reads as damage control.

How to answer a review you think is unfair

This is the situation owners get wrong most often, and understandably, because it is genuinely annoying. The instinct is to correct the record in public with the full account of what happened.

It does not work. A future customer reading a long rebuttal sees an argument and a business that argues, whatever the merits. They rarely conclude that the reviewer was wrong, because they have no way to judge.

What works is short: acknowledge the experience fell short, state plainly that you would like to put it right, and give a way to make contact. You look reasonable, which is the only thing the reply can achieve. If the review breaches policy it also gets reported, separately and quietly.

Questions

What people ask

Do you post replies directly or send them to me?

Either. Some owners want to approve everything, particularly early on, and some want it handled. Negative reviews are always worth a quick word with you first, because you know what happened and I do not.

Should I reply to every review?

Yes, including the one-line positive ones. It costs a sentence and it is visible to everyone reading afterwards.

Can a bad review be removed?

Only if it breaches Google's policies: spam, a competitor, offensive content, or someone who was never a customer. Being unfair is not grounds for removal, and I will tell you which one yours is rather than raising your hopes.

How fast should I reply?

Within a few days. Fast enough to look attentive, not so fast that a negative reply is written while you are still annoyed.

Answer the people watching

Tell me what is going on and I will tell you whether this is what you actually need. No pitch deck and no pressure.
